Serangan Serangan Surf Spot The left-hand reef break at Serangan is best at mid-tide. It offers smooth rides over a shallow rock shelf. Intermediate surfers love it for its reliability. Nearby, coral gardens are home to hawksbill turtles all year. Learning to surf in Bali at Serangan means eco-friendly lessons. Schools use soft-top boards to protect the reef. They teach about tidal patterns and turtle nesting seasons. Surfers leave with better skills and a love for Bali’s coast. Types of waves: Beginner Intermediate Advanced

headings: East coast rhythm, soft peaks and glassy reef rides
sections.text: Sanur, Bali East coast rhythm, soft peaks and glassy reef rides Despite its peaceful location on Bali’s east coast, Sanur’s surf speaks louder than words. This 5-kilometer stretch is perfect for all skill levels since it blends tough reefs with gentle sandy beaches. Tanjung Sari offers gentle, beginner-friendly peaks, while Hyatt Reef offers rhythmic right-handers on mid-high tides. For intermediates seeking tighter carves, Sanur Reef raises the ante. A local tip? For the smoothest waves, schedule your workouts with the tides.

Hyatt Reef Tanjung Sari Hyatt Reef The Right-Hander Rhythm This reef break is famous for its clockwork right-handers during mid-to-high tide. Our team suggests: 3-4ft swell range for clean wall sections, morning sessions to avoid afternoon crosswinds, and channel entry near the concrete marker Types of waves: Beginner Intermediate Advanced Tanjung Sari Surf Site With its three peaks, mellow rollers up north (all tides), faster rights in the center (mid tide), and left/right peaks down south (low tide)—and soft waist-high waves, this sandy-bottom beach is perfect for novices. Sanur Reef presents a difficulty for intermediates due to its fluctuating take-off zones. Because more reef is exposed during spring low tides, cutbacks and controlled carves are ideal. Types of waves: Intermediate Advanced

headings: Keramas power and volcanic coastline, wrapped in tradition
sections.text: Gianyar, Bali Keramas power and volcanic coastline, wrapped in tradition Gianyar combines intense surf energy with Bali’s cultural core. Keramas is a prime example of how the island’s volcanic coastline generates some of its most powerful waves. Fast, hollow rides are provided by this sophisticated reef break, which is best experienced during the rainy season at mid-to-high tide. Prime circumstances include early glass-offs and ESE swells. You might get insider knowledge or perhaps a place on a jet ski drop if you respect the lineup.

Keramas Keramas Bali’s Premier Advanced Break Keramas surf, which offers fast, hollow waves best during the rainy season (November to March), is best suited for experienced riders. For glassy conditions, go before 10 AM, surf mid-to-high tide to avoid exposed reef, and aim for ESE swells (120–150°). Although KFC’s break ten minutes north is less packed, local excursions provide equipment and direction. Jet skis are frequently used. Be mindful of the lineup; you can receive reef recommendations from locals. Types of waves: Advanced

headings: Skill-matched wave picks, tested, surfed, and recommended
sections.text: Best Surfing Spots for Every Level Skill-matched wave picks, tested, surfed, and recommended Bali’s waves are for everyone, from beginners to pros. Our team tested many spots to make this skill-matched surf guide . Now, you can find waves that fit your skill level perfectly.

Beginner Intermediate Advanced Beginner Find Your Wave Beginners will love Dreamland Beach because it has tiny, sandy waves and easy-to-learn lessons from schools like Odyssey Surf. For first pop-ups, morning sessions provide calm conditions free from strong currents. “I stood on my first wave here, felt safe but challenged!” says Australian surfer Lena P. Other excellent places for beginners include Seminyak’s laid-back breaks with convenient rental access and Kuta Beach’s silky rollers. Intermediate Level Up Visit Medewi Beach, Bali’s famous left-hand point break, for longer rides. At mid-tide, its gentle 300-meter waves are great for practicing bottom turns and cutbacks. To help you improve, nearby surf camps even provide video analysis. Try Balian’s smooth beach break, which is open all day and has fewer visitors, or Keramas’ punchy reef at high tide for extra diversity. Advanced Expert Playground At hidden locations like Shipwrecks on Nusa Lembongan, which is best surfed by locals because of its shallow reef, experienced surfers seek out Bali’s unadulterated energy. Before the winds rise, Green Bowl gives glassy barrels to dawn patrols. The most reliable swells occur during the dry season, which runs from April to October. Some world-class breaks only last 90 minutes until circumstances change, so always check the tide charts.

headings: Easy ways to reach the beach and surf
sections.text: How to Get There Easy ways to reach the beach and surf Local knowledge is necessary to go to Bali’s surfing places. To locate reefs like Sanur, use landmarks like Pura Segara. Scooters are great; check the tires and rent from reliable stores. Plan ahead because coastal routes may close during the monsoon season. Ferries to Nusa Penida depart Sanur every day. Use live cameras from Balangan, Keramas, and Canggu to monitor swell and road access, and schedule your sessions according to the tide type.

sections.text: FAQ Surfing in Bali FAQ What's the best surf spot in Bali for beginners? Kuta Beach is great for beginners with its gentle waves. Kima Surf offers foam boards and reef shoes. Medewi’s long waves are perfect for improving after you learn the basics. When is the optimal time to surf in Bali? The west coast is best from April to October with swells of 3-8ft. Nusa Dua is better from November to March. Wait 48 hours after rain to avoid pollution, as Marthe from our team did. Are private surf lessons worth the extra cost? Group lessons are $35-$50 and build friendship. Private lessons are $75-$120 for personalized feedback. Our surf+yoga packages offer both. Naomi says daily yoga warm-ups helped her avoid injuries during her 7-day course. What critical safety rules do Bali surf schools enforce? Always use a leash and never drop your board sideways. Uluwatu’s reefs need precise timing. Red flags at Canggu mean only experts should surf. Our instructors check currents every hour. Why choose Medewi over crowded southern spots? Medewi has 300m rides for practicing turns without crowds. Surf 2 hours before high tide for the best waves. Wear water shoes for the slippery lava rock entry. It’s perfect after 5 sessions in Kuta. How does Balian Beach compare to Medewi? Balian has black sand and punchier waves, while Medewi has longer waves. Stay at Warung D’Balian Homestay, our instructors’ favorite. Weekdays are less crowded than weekends, according to our 2023 logs.

sections.text: Canggu Surf Sports

headings: Five beaches, endless breaks, and Bali’s surf scene
Best Spots for Beginners to Pros
sections.text: Complete Surf Guide to Canggu Five beaches, endless breaks, and Bali’s surf scene Once a quiet fishing community, Canggu today welcomes more than 500,000 surfers each year. From Echo Beach’s barrels to Batu Bolong’s gentle waves, its black sand beaches provide reef breaks for surfers of all skill levels. Families and remote workers coexist alongside surfers. Canggu, which is within walking distance and features views of rice fields, warungs, cafés, and co-working spaces, combines Bali’s surf culture with contemporary conveniences and communal living. Best Spots for Beginners to Pros Batu Bolong (Beginner) Berawa Beach (Intermediate) Echo Beach (Expert)

headings: Year-round waves and vibrant beach life
sections.text: General Info Year-round waves and vibrant beach life Top Surf Spots Surf Spot Level The seven kilometers of Canggu’s volcanic coastline are home to five different surf beaches: Echo, Batu Bolong, Berawa, Pererenan, and Nelayan. Each offers different conditions, ranging from strong reef breaks to gentle sand-bottom waves. Clean, head-high barrels are revealed by morning mid-tides, and year-round surf sessions are sustained by warm waters and seasonal swells. Beach clubs, board storage, and post-surf smoothies are all within easy reach of most breakers, which are accessible by scooter.

headings: Dry season brings the cleanest swells
sections.text: Best Time Dry season brings the cleanest swells Canggu offers two seasons of magical waves with a surf schedule that synchronizes with the tropical monsoons. For intermediates and pros, the dry season (May–October) offers reliable 4–8 foot swells and clear offshore winds. There are less people, warmer waters, and waves that are 2–4 feet friendly during the wet season, which runs from November to March. Before the afternoon rains arrive, astute surfers get up early, consult tidal charts, and take advantage of the smooth morning conditions.

headings: Shallow reefs, big crowds, and hidden rocks
sections.text: Warnings Shallow reefs, big crowds, and hidden rocks Canggu’s surf is rewarding. A fantastic session might become dangerous because to packed queues, strong rip currents, and sharp reefs. Recognize your risks: paddling wide maintains calm on crowded peaks like Batu Bolong, while reef shoes are helpful for shallow takeoffs like Echo Reef. Observe local customs by waiting your turn, apologizing frequently, and not snapping. Every lineup respects safe surfing.

headings: From calm shores to big waves
sections.text: Top Surf Spots in Canggu From calm shores to big waves There are eight different surf areas on Canggu’s five beaches, from barreling reefs at The Ledge to gentle rollers at Batu Bolong, suitable for surfers of all skill levels. While experienced surfers pursue swift, shallow rights at Rivermouth, beginners enjoy the sandy takeoffs. Bring the appropriate board, be aware of your tides, and observe the flow of the crowd. To get the best waves, use local charts and early mornings.

headings: Ideal for surfers of all skill levels
sections.text: Banjar Canggu Ideal for surfers of all skill levels Banjar Canggu has four surf zones for all skill levels. Early mornings are perfect for surfing here. Surf schools are near Batu Bolong Beach, and Echo Beach is great for photos. After surfing, try smoothie bowls at Crate Cafe, just a short walk from the beach.

headings: Beginner to Expert, All in One Spot
sections.text: Echo Beach Batu Bolong’s Channel Flow Berawa’s Triple-Layered Challenge Echo Beach Triple Threat Waves The Echo Beach Canggu surf scene is exciting. Beginners start at Stairs for easy waves. Advanced surfers love Rivermouth’s barrels during southwest swells. At mid-tide, the Sandbar’s A-frame peaks are perfect for practicing. Don’t miss the sunset photos from the southern rocks. Types of dives: Beginner Intermediate Advanced Batu Bolong’s Channel Flow Longboarder’s hidden playground Batu Bolong surf is known for its consistent waves. Mid-tide is the best time to surf here. Longboarders enjoy the calm inside section near the temple. Surf schools teach lessons here. Be careful of rips during outgoing tides. Types of waves: Beginner Intermediate Berawa’s Triple-Layered Challenge Beginner to Expert, All in One Spot Berawa Beach surf has zones for all levels. Start at The Peak for easy waves. Then, move to Middle Reef for faster waves. Experts head to The Bombie for big swells. Paddle out early to get a spot near Finns Recreation Club. After surfing, check out the board shops along Jalan Pantai Berawa. Types of waves: Beginner Intermediate Advanced

Batu Bolong, Canggu Perfect for longboarders and first-timers Batu Bolong is the best place for novices to learn in Canggu, where gentle surf meets volcanic rocks. Old Man’s Beach, which is just south, serves as a natural surf school, with knee-to-chest-high waves that break softly over soft sand, making it ideal for beginners. This beach is popular with surf schools because of its warm waters, gentle crashes, and angled takeoffs. To avoid the crowds and take advantage of the best learning environment, arrive before 7 AM. As abilities advance, local teachers advise adhering to lineup etiquette and switching to hybrid boards for greater control.

Old Man’s Beach Old Man’s Beach Your Wave-Riding Classroom Old Man’s Beach is Canggu’s beginner haven, with mellow knee- to chest-high waves breaking over soft sand, perfect for learning. Surf schools love it here: angled takeoffs teach control, soft wipeouts ease nerves, and warm water keeps you going. Arrive before 7 AM to beat the surf camp crowds and catch clean “golden hour” waves. Respect the lineup, upgrade to a hybrid board when ready, and keep the aloha spirit alive. Types of waves: Beginner Intermediate

headings: Gentle currents, colorful reefs, and beginner-friendly dives
sections.text: Best Surfing Spots for Every Level Gentle currents, colorful reefs, and beginner-friendly dives Canggu’s coast offers something for every skill level, from gentle beginner rollers at Batu Bolong to barreling rights at Echo Beach. At Batu Bolong, local teachers and 9’0″ foamies help beginners gain confidence. During incoming tide, intermediates move forward on funboards at Berawa’s top. At Echo’s Rivermouth, experts use shortboards and wetsuit tops approved by Jordy Lawler, to chase low-tide barrels.

Beginner Zones Intermediate Challenges Advanced Breaks Beginner Zones Find Your Wave Batu Bolong is perfect for newbies. Its waves are gentle and waist-high, giving you time to practice. Mojo Surf Canggu offers lessons here, with instructors cheering you on. Start with a 9’0″ mini-mal from local surf board rental shops. It’s stable and easy to handle. Lessons include GoPro footage to help you improve fast. Intermediate Challenges Level Up Berawa Beach ‘s peak break is for those ready for more. It offers 4-6ft rights that are great for practicing. Surf here during the last two hours of the incoming tide for better waves. Try a 7’2″ funboard for better control. The surf hotel in the Canggu area means you can surf early without crowds. Advanced Breaks Expert Playground Echo Beach ‘s Rivermouth is a challenge at low tide. It’s known for its hollow rights that require skill. Australian pro Jordy Lawler says it’s great for learning heavy barrels. Use a high-performance shortboard and a 3/2mm wetsuit top for protection.

headings: Skip the traffic, ride smart, and stay close to the surf
sections.text: How to Get There Skip the traffic, ride smart, and stay close to the surf Ngurah Rai Airport is just 13 miles from Batu Bolong. You can hire a private driver (IDR 350K/day) or rent a scooter (IDR 100K/day) for surf independence. To avoid traffic, arrive before 7 AM or after 9 PM. Stay at Lapoint Surf Camp for easy access to the beach, rentals, and board repairs, Drifter Surf Shop has you covered. Always wear a helmet and have cash on hand for parking.

sections.text: FAQ Surfing in Canggu FAQ Why is Canggu considered Bali's top surf destination? Canggu is known for its amazing waves and lively coastal vibe. It has black sand beaches with waves for all levels. You can find everything from powerful reef breaks to calm beach breaks, all near modern amenities. When is the best time for beginners to take surf lessons in Canggu? The best time for beginners is November to March. The waves are gentler then. Surf schools like Mojo Surf and Canggu Surf School offer lessons in the morning when it’s calm. What safety precautions are essential at Canggu's surf breaks? Always wear reef shoes at Echo Reef and Rivermouth. Check the tides to avoid rocks at low tide. Respect the rules at busy spots like the Sandbar. Lifeguards warn against strong currents at Echo Beach. Which Canggu surf spots work best for longboarders? Batu Bolong is great for longboarding with its gentle waves. Pererenan has right-hand walls for noseriding. But The Ledge is better for shortboarders and experts. How do tides affect surf conditions at Berawa Beach? Berawa’s breaks change with the 2.8m tidal range. The Peak is best at mid-tide. The Bombie’s barrels are for advanced riders at high tide. Surf camps like Odyssey Surf School give daily updates. Where can I find beginner-friendly surf camps in Canggu? Batu Bolong Beach has top surf camps for beginners. Rapture Surf Camp and Old Man’s Surf School offer great coaching and gear. What makes Echo Beach's surf breaks unique? Echo Beach has two breaks. Stairs is for experts with its barrels. The Sandbar is for intermediates. Enjoy coconut water and grilled mahi-mahi at “Tempo Doeloe” after surfing. Are there surfboard rental shops near Canggu's main breaks? Yes, Drifter Surf and Canggu Boardriders rent near Batu Bolong. For Rivermouth, bring your own or rent from Deus Ex Machina’s Temple of Enthusiasm. How do I avoid crowds at Canggu's popular surf spots? Surf early, from 6 to 8 AM, to avoid crowds. Advanced surfers chase hollow tubes at Mawi, and experts ride the legendary 300-meter barrels at Desert Point. Whether mellow or massive, there’s a perfect wave waiting along Lombok’s shores.

headings: Mid-tide peaks with chill Kuta vibes
sections.text: Gerupuk Bay Ekas Beach Seger Beach Mawi Gerupuk Bay Beginner waves, pro guides Gerupuk Bay is where surf lessons turn into real adventures. Local instructors, blending traditional “juru selam” knowledge with modern tips, guide you through calm waves at Inside Right or the faster breaks at Outside Right. Don-Don’s mellow peaks and Tanjung Aan’s long lefts offer something for everyone. With small class sizes, you’ll build confidence and flow with every ride. Surf spot level: Beginner Intermediate Ekas Beach Smooth rides and fast lefts Ekas Beach is where calm waves teach and wild ones thrill. Inside Ekas offers smooth 3–5ft waves for beginners, while Outside Ekas delivers deep, fast lefts for the advanced. Local guides say tides shape the experience, and early sessions beat winds. A protected paddle-out channel and shifting wave moods make Ekas both a teacher and a test. Surf spot level: Beginner Intermediate Seger Beach Mid-tide peaks with chill Kuta vibes As golden hour hits the reef, Seger Beach becomes more than a surf spot, it’s a classroom for timing, speed, and wave reading. With punchy lefts for intermediates and faster rights for the advanced, it’s where skill levels rise. Mid-tide is ideal, reef booties are a must, and after your ride, Kuta’s warungs and massages bring the perfect wind-down. Surf spot level: Beginner Intermediate Mawi Barreling drops for thrill seekers Mawi brings strong waves, fast drops, and big barrels that test your skills. On 6–8ft swells, it’s an A-frame dream for pros, while beginners can stick to the softer shoulders. Easterly winds polish the faces, but strong rips and reef hazards demand caution. Follow channel flags, surf mid-tide, and always respect the break. Mawi rewards boldness, but only if you’re ready. Surf spot level: Intermediate Advanced

Desert Point (Bangko-Bangko) Lombok's Barrel Factory Desert Point is Lombok’s most iconic and challenging wave. This world-class left-hand reef break offers 20-second barrels when SW swells, ESE winds, and mid-to-high tides align. It’s only for experienced surfers and demands respect, both from the ocean and the local village. Visit between May–September, follow local rules, and prepare for one of surfing’s ultimate tests.

headings: Mix of mellow and sharp waves
sections.text: Are Guling Senggigi Belongas Are Guling Mix of mellow and sharp waves At Are Guling, you get two waves in one spot. The right reef offers playful walls for intermediate surfers, while the left reef is faster and hollow, perfect for advanced riders chasing barrels. Surf it best between November and April, and aim for morning sessions. Respect the tides, wear reef booties, and team up with local boats for safety and tips. Surf spot level: Intermediate Advanced Senggigi Chill surf meets coastal culture Senggigi offers a mellow surf escape on Lombok’s north coast. Its calm bay and soft beach breaks are perfect for longboarders, SUP riders, and beginners finding their balance. Morning waves invite smooth rides, while afternoons reveal Sasak village life, spicy ayam taliwang, and local crafts. It’s where you ride the ocean early, then soak in culture by sunset. Surf spot level: Intermediate Advanced Belongas Remote reef playground Belongas boasts five unique breaks, from gentle waves at Kids Point to the powerful tubes of Outside Left. Make sure to check the surf report for Kuta Lombok before heading out. The 90-minute boat ride from Awang Harbor is worth it for these waves. Start at DonDon’s right-handers for some fun practice. Waist-high waves here are perfect for learning cutbacks. As the swells grow, move to the Main Peak for its fast, racing sections. Advanced surfers will love Outside Left’s huge barrels. These waves can reach triple overhead and break over a shallow reef. Local boat captains can guide you to the best spots on the Lombok surf spots map. Visit between April and October for the best waves. Surf spot level: Intermediate Advanced

Ekas Outside throws clean lefts near limestone cliffs. Mawi’s A-frame peaks shift with the tide, fun at high, barreling at mid, and heavy at low. These breaks reward good timing, positioning, and growing confidence. Advance Spots Zones Power and precision only for seasoned pros. Lombok’s top surf spots for advanced riders include Desert Point and Senggigi. Desert Point is famous for its long, barreling lefts, best with SW swells and mid-tide. Senggigi delivers powerful A-frame peaks over coral, working well on NW winter swells. Both demand skill, timing, and local knowledge. These breaks offer pure Indonesian energy for those ready to take on the challenge.

sections.text: FAQ Surfing in Lombok FAQ When is the best time to surf in Lombok? Lombok has waves all year, but the seasons change things. The dry season (May-September) has offshore winds and big waves on the west coast. The wet season (November-March) brings big waves to the south. Don’t miss the “bau nyale” festival in February or March. It’s a chance to see local culture while surfing. How does Lombok's surfing compare to Bali? Lombok has great waves without the crowds. It has unique reefs that create different levels of breaks. The surf ladder system helps you move from easy bays to tough reefs. The tides here (2-4m) change the breaks every day. This is different from Bali’s more steady conditions. Do I need a guide for Lombok surf spots? Yes, guides are key for reef breaks. They know the tides, like Mawi’s calm high tide and its low tide challenges. They also help avoid fishing boats at Gerupuk and find the best spots at Ekas Outside. Most surf camps include guides in their packages. Which Lombok surf spots work best for beginners? Beginners love Gerupuk Inside for its long right-handers. Seger Beach has two peaks, one for beginners. Ekas Inside is great for first-timers with its safety boat. How do tides affect Lombok's surf conditions? The 4m tidal range changes the breaks a lot. Mawi goes from fun waves to hard barrels with the tide. Gerupuk Outside is fast at mid tide. Check the tide charts. Some spots, like Desert Point, only work in a small window. Can I reach Desert Point without a 4x4 vehicle? You can try on a scooter, but it’s tough. Sekotong’s roads are rough. Most surf camps offer boat rides from Kuta. Desert Point needs the right conditions for its famous waves. Locals say it’s either on or off. What's the best way to access Lombok surf spots from Bali? The fastest way is a 25-minute flight to Lombok International Airport (LOP). It’s close to Kuta. You can also take a 4-hour ferry from Padang Bai to Lembar Harbor. Once in Lombok, rent a big scooter for the mountain roads. Surf camps offer daily transport to many spots. Are there surf camps offering yoga and cultural experiences? Yes! Mocean Resort and others offer yoga, cultural tours, and surf lessons. They also have video analysis and reef boot rentals. You can even go on a bau nyale fishing trip. Kuta has modern lodges, while Gerupuk offers local stays. What safety gear do I need for Lombok's reef breaks? Reef boots are a must at most spots, except Seger. Wear a 2mm neoprene top for long sessions at Ekas Outside. Surf schools provide helmets for tricky spots like Senggigi. Always surf with a buddy. The currents can be strong at spots like Gerupuk Outside. How do I choose between Kuta and Gerupuk surf accommodations? Kuta has a lively scene and surf shops. It’s great for those who love to party. Gerupuk is quieter, near five breaks, but it’s a bit further north. Consider starting in Kuta for Seger Beach, then move to Gerupuk for more challenging waves.

sections.text: Nusa Lembongan Home to perfect reef breaks surfable straight from the shore Explore Nusa Lembongan’s unique surf spots, where top waves meet tropical ease. The island’s nusa lembongan surf sites line its southwestern coast. They offer reef breaks for every skill level. Beachfront villas are just steps from Playgrounds and Lacerations, ideal for early morning surf.

Playgrounds Lacerations Playgrounds Surf Site Nusa Lembongan’s playgrounds are an A-frame paradise, with waves of all skill levels breaking over a sandy reef. The best shape is provided by mid-tides (1.8–2.4 m), with lefts and rights ideal for carving. For best conditions, surf 90 minutes before high tide. Pros attack the hollows, intermediates adore 4–6 feet, and beginners ride 2–4 feet. On pushing water, stay 20 meters clear of south-end rocks and check the tides. Types of waves: Beginner Intermediate Advanced Lacerations Surf Site The well-known Nusa Lembongan break Lacerations got its name from a 2003 wipeout that left a surfer with twelve stitches, a tale that is being remembered today. During mid-tide southwest swells (May–September), this swift, hollow wave peaks with 4–6 foot sets and breaks over shallow coral. Bring a spotter, ride a 6’0″–6’6″ board, and wear booties. Higher tides lessen the blow, whereas lower tides increase the danger. Types of waves: Advanced

Razors Cliffside Thrills and Tight Lines Lembongan’s expert surfers love Razors because of its strong bowl sections and quick, hollow lefts. Head-high to double overhead waves necessitate deep takeoffs and precise timing. It’s more reliable and less busy than playgrounds, and it’s best from April to October. Every Razors session seems like a fast-paced, precision-driven movie ride because to the stunning cliffside, which heightens the excitement.

Shipwrecks Shipwrecks Surf Spot Legian stands out as a top beginner spot, with mellow waves ideal for learning. The Padma Peak section has waist-high waves for mastering pop-ups. The southern zones offer bigger waves for those looking to improve. Local instructors say the best time to surf is in the mid-morning when the winds are calm. Types of waves: Intermediate Advanced

Advanced Expert Playground At hidden locations like Shipwrecks on Nusa Lembongan, which is best surfed by locals because of its shallow reef, experienced surfers seek out Bali’s unadulterated energy. sections.text: FAQ Surfing in Nusa Lembongan FAQ Why is Nusa Lembongan considered a top surfing destination? Nusa Lembongan is a top spot for surfing. It has world-class reef breaks and warm tropical water. The surf community is laid-back. Features like offshore pontoons make it easy to get in line. It’s great for all skill levels, from beginners to experts. How do I get to Nusa Lembongan from Bali? Fast boats from Sanur or Serangan Harbor in Bali take 30–45 minutes. Companies like Rocky Fast Cruise or Scoot Cruises handle your luggage and boards. They also transfer you to your accommodation. Stay at least 2 nights to enjoy the island’s surf spots and relaxed vibe. When is the best time to surf in Nusa Lembongan? The best months are April–October. This time has consistent swells and offshore winds. Peak season (June–August) has bigger waves but more people. Shoulder seasons (April–May, September–October) offer good surf and peace. Avoid November–March because of rainy-season runoff. What safety precautions should I take while surfing here? Be careful of sharp reefs, rip currents, and underwater obstacles. Always surf with local guides. Avoid Shipwrecks on big swells and check tide charts. Wear reef boots and don’t push your limits at advanced breaks like Lacerations. What are the top surf spots in Nusa Lembongan? – Shipwrecks: Right-hand reef break, best at mid-high tide (strong currents). – Razors: Fast left-hander perfect for improving technique. – Lacerations: Hollow barrels for experts only. – Playgrounds: Gentle A-frames ideal for beginners. Time sessions around tides and avoid midday crowds for the best experience. Can I surf at Nusa Ceningan? Yes! The Ceningan surf spot, near Mahana Point’s cliffside bar, offers a lesser-crowded left-hander. Bring a rash guard for cooler water, and enjoy crystal-clear waves perfect for action photos. After surfing, grab a sunset drink at Mahana or explore Nusa Ceningan’s attractions like the Blue Lagoon.

Sumbawa rewards the surfers who make the effort to get here. Why Choose Sumbawa for Surfing The waves stay wonderfully uncrowded, paddle out at the right time and you might share a world-class break with only a handful of others, or even have it to yourself. The island is split into two main surf zones: West Sumbawa, home to heavy hitters like Scar Reef, Supersuck, and Yoyos, and East Sumbawa, ruled by the legendary A-frame at Lakey Peak. Between them you’ll find every kind of wave, from sharp, mechanical barrels to gentle, forgiving reef breaks. Add warm water year-round, affordable food and stays, and that unmistakable “islands as they used to be” feeling, and it’s easy to see why Sumbawa has become a bucket-list surf trip.

headings: What to Bring for a Sumbawa Surf Trip
When Is the Best Time to Surf Sumbawa?
sections.text: Here's the practical stuff that makes a Sumbawa surf trip smooth, safe, and stress-free. Simple Tips What Need to Bring Before Surfing When the Best Time to Surf What to Bring for a Sumbawa Surf Trip Sumbawa is remote, and surf shops are few and far between, so come self-sufficient. Bring the right boards for reef breaks (and a spare if you can), plus backup leashes, fins, and plenty of wax. Reef booties are a must for shallow, low-tide sessions, and a rash guard, reef-safe sunscreen, and a basic first-aid kit for coral scrapes are all wise additions. Since the waves pack a punch, pack for power rather than for gentle beach days. When Is the Best Time to Surf Sumbawa? The dry season, roughly May to September (with April and October as solid shoulder months), is prime time. This is when consistent southwest swells and offshore trade winds groom the reefs into their best form, with June and July often the most reliable for size. If you’re a beginner or intermediate, the wet season (November to March) can actually be lovely with smaller, mellower waves, lighter winds, glassy mornings, and even thinner crowds. Whatever the season, dawn patrol usually serves up the cleanest conditions before the wind picks up.
Here are the breaks that put Sumbawa on the map. Top Surf Spots

Western Spots Northern Rights Supersuck Scar Reef Yo-yos Tropical Northern Rights A faster right-hand reef break in the Kertasari area, just a short scooter ride from where we’re based in Moro Bay. It works best on mid to high tide with a clean swell and suits intermediate to advanced surfers. Mind the rocks in the line-up, and you’ll be rewarded with punchy, uncrowded rights. Surf Spot Level: Intermediate Advance Supersuck The name says it all. Supersuck is one of Indonesia’s longest, most intense left-hand tube breaks, unfurling over a shallow, live coral reef. It only fires on solid swells, but when it does, you’ll see surfers link multiple barrels on a single wave. This one is strictly for advanced surfers with good tube technique. Surf Spot Level: Intermediate Advance Scar Reef A powerful, world-class left-hander often compared to G-Land, Scar Reef throws big, walling barrels down a long reef and handles serious size. It’s the main attraction of West Sumbawa and a magnet for experienced surfers chasing hollow, high-consequence waves. Advanced riders only. Surf Spot Level: Advance Yo-yos A versatile break with both left and right options, Yoyos is one of Sumbawa’s rare quality right-handers and is best surfed at mid to high tide. Consistent and swell-hungry, it suits confident intermediate and advanced surfers, and it’s picked up enough of a reputation to feature on the competition radar. Surf Spot Level: Intermediate Advance Tropical Just around the headland from Yoyos, Tropical (Tropicals) is probably the softest wave in West Sumbawa, breaking beside a beautiful white-sand beach. It offers both lefts and rights and, depending on the wind, can be a fun, more forgiving alternative. Surf Spot Level: Beginner Intermediate Advance

Eastern Spots Lakey Peak Nunggas Periscopes Maci Point Lakey Peak The crown jewel. Lakey Peak is a near-perfect A-frame that peels both left and right off a tight reef peak, with multiple barrel sections on dry-season swells. The left is the longer, more celebrated ride; the right is shorter, faster, and more technical. It’s world-class and expert territory, so know your limits before you paddle over. Surf Spot Level: Intermediate Advance Nunggas Often called the main intermediate wave of the area, Nunggas (Nungas) is a long, workable left-hand point that peels with distance over raw power. The drop is easier than Lakey’s, making it a favourite for improvers and hotdogging surfers, while advanced riders enjoy it most in the dry season. Surf Spot Level: Beginner Intermediate Periscopes A Sumbawa legend and a rare right-hander, Periscopes is a boat ride around the point north of Lakey. It offers a high, tight barrel over a relatively safe reef platform with a clean exit into the channel. It starts firing at higher tide and gets steep on bigger days Surf Spot Level: Intermediate Advance Maci Point A right-hander breaking over a coral rock ledge, Maci Point works best on higher tide and picks up plenty of swell. It’s often a great call when Lakey is small, and trips out here can turn into a fun surfari-style day, sometimes with a bit of fishing along the way. Surf Spot Level: Intermediate Advance
Surf Spot Levels Here’s a simple way to match Sumbawa’s waves to your ability. Remember that levels shift with swell and tide, so always check conditions on the day.

Beginner Spots Intermediate Spots Advanced Spots Beginner Spots Tropical is the softest wave in West Sumbawa, with lefts and rights next to a white-sand beach. Nunggas, on the east coast near Lakey, is a long, workable left that suits progressing surfers on smaller days. Close to Mocean, Middle Reef has softer take-offs and mellow shoulders, which is where our coaches take beginners for surf lessons . Intermediate Spots Tropical, Yoyos (on smaller swells), Nunggas, and Periscopes reward confident intermediates with longer, faster rides and gentler sections than the heavy stuff. These are the breaks to work on your turns and get comfortable on reef. Advanced Spots This is where Sumbawa truly shines. Scar Reef, Supersuck, Lakey Peak, and Lakey Pipe deliver fast, hollow, powerful barrels over shallow reef for seasoned surfers. Bring your best boards, your booties, and your A-game.

sections.text: FAQ Sumbawa Surf FAQ Do I need to hire a surf guide in Sumbawa? It’s highly recommended, especially for your first visit or for the heavier reef breaks. A good guide reads the tides and swell, knows which spot suits the day’s conditions, and keeps you safe over shallow coral. Even confident surfers save time and score better waves with local knowledge on their side. Are there surfboard rentals available in Sumbawa? Yes, many surf resorts, camps, and beachside shops rent boards, and some offer lessons for beginners. That said, Sumbawa is remote and selection can be limited, so if you ride a specific board or need a gun for bigger days, it’s smart to bring your own — plus backup fins, leashes, and wax. How many days should I spend surfing in Sumbawa? We’d suggest at least five to seven days to account for travel time and to give yourself a good window of swell and tides. A week lets you settle into the rhythm, explore multiple breaks, and enjoy a rest day or two without feeling rushed. Longer is even better if your schedule allows. What should I pack for a surfing trip to Sumbawa? Bring your boards and plenty of spares (leashes, fins, wax), reef booties for shallow sessions, a rash guard, and reef-safe sunscreen. Add a basic first-aid kit for coral scrapes, a dry bag, and light, quick-drying clothing. Since supplies are limited on the island, it pays to arrive well prepared. Are there accommodations near Sumbawa's surf spots? Absolutely. From simple surf camps and homestays to comfortable beachfront resorts, both coasts have places to stay close to the waves. On the west coast, being based near the Kertasari and Moro Bay breaks means you can check the surf before breakfast — which is exactly what makes staying with us so convenient.

There's no better feeling than waking up to the sound of the ocean. sections.text: General Info Year-round waves and vibrant beach life Bingin Beach Area Bombie Area The Peak Area Surf Site Impossibles Nyang Nyang Area The seven kilometers of Canggu’s volcanic coastline are home to five different surf beaches: Echo, Batu Bolong, Berawa, Pererenan, and Nelayan. Each offers different conditions, ranging from strong reef breaks to gentle sand-bottom waves. headings: A short stretch with a full range of challenges
sections.text: Surf Sites in Bingin Beach Area A short stretch with a full range of challenges Just minutes apart, Bingin and Dreamland offer two sides of the surf coin. Train on Dreamland’s soft, sandy waves, then graduate to Bingin’s precise reef barrels. This stretch is ideal for improving surfers, start your day with mellow turns, then test your timing on Bingin’s 50-meter lefts. From April to October, it’s a natural skill-building circuit in the Bukit.

Tomas Beach Temples Tomas Beach Surf Spot Also known as Labuan Sait, Tomas Beach gives surfers a chance to grow, from playful 1–3 ft shorebreaks to Padang Padang’s 12 ft barrels just offshore. Start small, then level up as your confidence builds. Morning tides are great for learners, while advanced surfers chase late-day perfection. Locals even use rip currents as shortcuts past the break. Types of dives: Reef Temples Surf Spot Temples offers the best spiritual surfing where surges from the Indian Ocean meet limestone cliffs. The “ombak suci” (holy waves) beneath Uluwatu Temple provide strong lefts, steep takeoffs, and swift barrels. Neap tides encourage intermediates, while spring tides are best for pros. Don’t forget that this isn’t just a break. It is the meeting point of Balinese heritage and ocean vitality. Types of dives: Drift Reef Ocean Pool and Wall

headings: Where tide charts and moon phases
sections.text: Surf Sites In The Bombie Area Where tide charts and moon phases These two iconic waves put even the most experienced surfers to the test when Bali’s southern shore comes alive. From Outside Corner’s swift technical barrels to Bombie’s imposing walls, this is Uluwatu at its strongest, when indecision is not an option and tide charts and moon phases are important.

The Bombie Outside Corner The Bombie Surf Spot When swells reach 8 feet, the Bombie, Bali’s big-wave monster, breaks over a small reef; in the winter, it frequently reaches 15 to 20 feet vertically. For true chargers, it’s a wave with 45-second rides over connected parts. Local boat captains are aware of the optimal moon-phase entry, and jet ski aids are essential on big days. You commit before the wave even rises; you don’t just paddle into Bombie. Outside Corner Surf Spot Old Man’s Beach is Canggu’s beginner haven, with mellow knee- to chest-high waves breaking over soft sand, perfect for learning. Surf schools love it here: angled takeoffs teach control, soft wipeouts ease nerves, and warm water keeps you going. Arrive before 7 AM to beat the surf camp crowds and catch clean “golden hour” waves. Respect the lineup, upgrade to a hybrid board when ready, and keep the aloha spirit alive.

headings: Plan, paddle, and perform on Uluwatu’s technical terrain
sections.text: Surf Sites In The Peak Area Plan, paddle, and perform on Uluwatu’s technical terrain Bali’s experienced surfers hone their craft on these renowned reef breaks. Timing the tides and reading the reef are crucial for everything from the fast takeoffs at The Peak to the speed runs at Racetrack and the 500-meter barrels for Impossibles. This is not only surfing, but it’s about planning, precision, and mastering the ocean’s rhythm.

The Peak Racetrack The Peak Surf Spot The Peak is a training ground for locals. It has steep takeoffs over a shallow reef, needing quick reflexes. Waves change, turning left-handers into A-frames with the tides. Mid-tide is best here, offering depth for safer wipeouts. Use your shortest board. Watch locals ride through seemingly impossible sections. Racetrack Surf Spot For surfers who are intermediate to advanced, the racetrack’s 300 meters of fast, continuous walls are ideal. When the parts line up and the pace increases, hit it on an outgoing mid-tide. To keep ahead of the reef, take off a little bit toward the waterway. The greatest time to ride without crowds is in the morning. You’ll read The Peak more effectively if you master Racetrack; they’re sister breaks designed for advancement.

headings: Endurance Rides for Skilled and Precise Surfers
sections.text: Surf Sites Impossibles Endurance Rides for Skilled and Precise Surfers For experienced surfers, Impossibles is a paradise, with 500-meter rides on smooth, swift walls. During the “magic hour,” when winds decrease, west waves transform the reef into a smooth, machine-like wave. It takes astute timing, location, and tapering swell reading to succeed here. Make use of Villa Bayuh Sabbha as a blueprint for your lineup. Cleaner sets come with dawn; paddle early and keep an eye out for black lines on the horizon.

headings: Glassy mornings and raw solitude below the cliffs
sections.text: Surf Sites in Nyang Nyang Area Glassy mornings and raw solitude below the cliffs Hikers can enjoy uncrowded waves in the cliff-backed breaks of Nyang Nyang, which are remote and unadulterated. This location, which pairs glassy mornings with northwest swells, is best from May to September. These waves are for surfers looking for seclusion and great lines outside of the regular Uluwatu circuit, so bring reef booties, patience, and an adventurous spirit.

sections.text: FAQ Surfing in Uluwatu FAQ Why is Bingin Beach called "the perfect barrel classroom"? Bingin Beach is known for its mechanical lefts. These waves break over a shallow reef, making it perfect for learning barrel-riding. Local guides teach timing and positioning here, even on moderate swells. Can beginners surf at Dreamland Beach? Yes, beginners can surf at Dreamland Beach. The waves near the shore are gentle, making it great for learning. Move to the southern end for more challenging waves. How does Tomas Beach accommodate different skill levels? Tomas Beach has two sides. Beginners can enjoy waist-high waves near the stairs. For experts, there are powerful right-handers at the Padang Padang tube. Local instructors teach how to navigate rip currents. What makes temple-area surfing spiritually significant? Surfing at Uluwatu Temple is special. The cliff geography creates unique A-frame peaks. Surf during neap tides when priests bless the waters, and respect the local customs. When should advanced surfers target The Bombie? Advanced surfers should surf The Bombie when swells are over 8ft and tides are low. Local boat captains help time the best entry. You’ll find powerful waves here. How do I sync sessions between The Peak and Racetrack? Sync sessions at The Peak and Racetrack with the right tide. When the tide is 1.4m and winds are ESE, the waves align. Start at The Peak and ride to Racetrack for long rides. What’s the secret to conquering Impossibles? Surf Impossibles during west swells of 5-7ft. Use the “Villa Bayuh Sabbha alignment” to find the best spot. You’ll catch a series of wedges for long rides. How do I access Nyang Nyang’s hidden coves safely? Access Nyang Nyang’s coves 90 minutes before high tide. Use a wind compass and watch for the “green flash” to find the best spot. You’ll find empty lineups in the northern coves. Which surf schools in Uluwatu offer expert-guided sessions? Uluwatu Surf School and Dreamsea Surf Camp offer expert sessions. They teach reef-readiness, including tidal timing and unique paddle techniques. What’s the best season for intermediate surfers in Uluwatu? April–October offers warm water and consistent swells. May and September provide great waves with fewer crowds. How do I respect local etiquette at Uluwatu’s surf breaks? Respect local etiquette by following “banjar” rules. Give priority to local surfers during dawn patrol. Never drop in and avoid sacred coral formations. Surf schools provide cultural briefings and a “selendang” for temple sessions.

Surf West Sumbawa’s Legendary Waves at Mocean Beach Resort
sections.text: West Sumbawa, stretched between Lombok and Flores, feels wild yet welcoming, larger than Bali but quieter and more grounded. Life here moves with the tides. Beyond the surf, there’s reef snorkeling, island-hopping, and hikes to hidden waterfalls. You might meet whale sharks in Saleh Bay or stroll through local markets where life flows slow and sincere. From May to October, the dry season brings clear waves and golden light. Sumbawa is growing but still deeply local, best explored by motorbike, where each journey connects you to the island’s sea, trails, and kind-hearted people. Quick List: The Best Things to Do in West Sumbawa Surf Northern Rights, Middle Reef and Dirty Hippies on the west coast Snorkel or dive West Sumbawa’s reefs, including manta dives at Ju-Ju’s Jackpot Trek to Agal Waterfall (full day) or swim at Kalela Waterfall (half day) Island-hop and snorkel on the Three Island Tour Canoe Danau Lebo lake near Taliwang Watch sarong weaving and seaweed farming in local villages See whale sharks in Saleh Bay, a trip east into central Sumbawa Eat nasi goreng, martabak and fresh grilled fish at local warungs Surf West Sumbawa’s Legendary Waves at Mocean Beach Resort West Sumbawa offers world class breaks for surfers seeking consistent waves, fresh winds, and a relaxed pace. The coastline stretches from quiet coves to dramatic cliffs, offering long, clean waves that suit all skill levels. Northern Rights Surf Break Northern Rights sits just in front of Mocean Beach Resort and throws a bit more punch than its neighbors. It’s a right-hander with steeper faces and tighter sections—best tackled on a mid to high tide when the lines stack up clean. Not a wave for cruising; it rewards commitment and sharp turns, especially when the wind swings offshore and the crowd stays light. Middle Reef Surf Break Middle Reef, tucked between Northern Rights and Dirty Hippies, is your go-to for warm-ups and beginner sessions. Softer takeoffs, mellow shoulders, and a forgiving pace make it ideal for beginner surf lessons or just catching a few cruisers before the real push. It’s the kind of spot that lets you build confidence without getting worked. Dirty Hippies Surf Break Dirty Hippies is a laid-back left about a 15-minute walk down the beach. Easier than Northern Rights, it offers a smoother ride with longer walls and a slower tempo. Perfect for flowy lines, relaxed cutbacks, and soaking up the scenery when the tide’s right and the wind plays nice. Stay a short walk from all three breaks. See our Sumbawa surf camp . Go Snorkeling or Diving Around Sumbawa Island Slip into Sumbawa’s warm, crystal-clear waters and explore vibrant coral gardens teeming with reef fish. West Sumbawa’s pristine reefs remain largely untouched, perfect for small-group excursions guided by local experts who ensure you experience the island’s serene and unspoiled underwater world. Whale Sharks in Saleh Bay (Central Sumbawa) Saleh Bay, on the north coast of central Sumbawa, is known for whale sharks that feed near the fishing platforms (bagan). It is several hours by road east of West Sumbawa, so most visitors go on an overnight trip. Small-group tours keep the encounters calm and respectful. Closer to home, our snorkel trips and daily fun dives leave from the beach in front of the resort. Trek to Waterfalls and Walk the Rice Fields Beyond the waves, West Sumbawa offers serene treks to Agal Waterfall and scenic rice field walks. Guided excursions will lead you through lush trails, past cascading pools, and across vibrant paddies where local farmers work their fields. These peaceful journeys provide a refreshing contrast to surf days, letting you connect with Sumbawa’s natural beauty while immersing yourself in its quiet, rural scenery. Book a guided waterfall trip from the resort. Island Hopping on the Three Island Tour Spend a full day on the water visiting three small islets off the coast, with snorkeling over coral reefs and stops on quiet beaches. Divers can also book a two-tank boat trip to Kenawa. Ask about the Three Island Tour . Lakes and Viewpoints: Danau Lebo and Kopi Langit Canoe across Danau Lebo, a calm lake near Taliwang where local fishermen cast their nets, or hike up to Kopi Langit, a coffee-plantation viewpoint over the jungle hills, then cool off at Ai Mual waterfall on the way back. Discover Local Villages and Culture In West Sumbawa, time moves slow, moving with the tide and the fields. Travelers are greeted with smiles at roadside stalls, and children wave to passerby. For those wondering what to do beyond the beaches, village life is a gentle introduction. Markets, Traditions, and Respectful Travel West Sumbawa markets come alive in the early morning, vendors call out over baskets of fresh fish, spices, and produce. Villages like Lamunga and Moteng preserve traditional weaving and eco culture. Across West Sumbawa, modest dress and respectful behavior aren’t just appreciated—they’re the key to real connection, opening doors to a culture built on sincerity, tradition, and quiet pride. Feast on Local Sumbawa Cuisine After surfing or exploring Sumbawa island, enjoy food that’s fresh, simple, and made with care. Tasting local flavors is a must-do here, from warm rice and bright chilies to juicy tropical fruit. Warungs, Fresh Seafood, and Market Finds Cozy warungs serve nasi goreng, mie goreng, and martabak, while some restaurants like Mutiara by Mocean offer international dishes, and fresh fish prepared with local spices. For those exploring local markets, papaya, bananas, and coconut water highlight Sumbawa’s tropical bounty. Planning Your Sumbawa Trip The journey from Denpasar, Bali is seamless. Regular flights are available to West Sumbawa. From Lombok, options include a short flight or a combined land-and-sea route, with coastal pickups ready on arrival. When to Go The dry season is from May to October. Expect sunny days, steady winds, and clear trails. The surfing is best between April and October. At this time, waterfalls are flowing but still reachable. November to April is rainy, making hills lush and the air humid. Roads can get tricky, and some small services might stop. Getting Around Once in West Sumbawa, travel by car, scooter, or boat can be arranged through resorts and local vendors. Keep mindful of currents during your stay, dress modestly off the beach, and respect local customs. By mixing surf sessions, snorkeling, and village visits, your trip balances adventure, relaxation, and cultural connection, creating a seamless Sumbawa experience. How Many Days You Need Give West Sumbawa at least four nights. That is enough for two or three surf or dive days, one waterfall trip and a slow day at the beach. A week lets you add the islands, Danau Lebo and a rest day for the weather. Getting here from Bali or Lombok? See every route to Sumbawa . Where to Stay in Sumbawa For a surf-focused getaway, staying close to the waves and nature is key. Mocean Beach Resort in West Sumbawa offers luxury accommodations at 3 world-class surf breaks. Guests enjoy comfortable rooms, meals, snacks, and a relaxed atmosphere designed for both surf sessions and downtime. sections.text: FAQ Sumbawa Travel FAQ Is Sumbawa worth visiting? Yes, if you like surf, reefs and quiet roads. Sumbawa is bigger than Bali and far less developed, so you get uncrowded waves, empty beaches and waterfalls without the crowds. What is the best time to visit Sumbawa? May to October is dry season, with sunny days, steady surf and clear water. November to April brings rain, greener hills and fuller waterfalls. How do I get to Sumbawa from Bali? The quickest way is a direct flight from Bali to Sumbawa Besar (SWQ). You can also fly to Lombok and take the hourly ferry from Kayangan to Poto Tano. Where should I stay in West Sumbawa? From here, Mocean offers a seamless private transfer service around 2 hours and 15 minutes of scenic driving through the stunning landscapes of West Sumbawa. The route is often highlighted in travel to Sumbawa Utama guides, known for its dramatic hillsides, winding coastal views, and untouched countryside. Along the way you’ll pass through traditional villages and lush greenery, giving you a glimpse of local life before arriving at the serene setting of Mocean Resort.

Enjoy scenic island views as you arrive by boat Ferry Pickup from Poto Tano If you prefer to travel by sea, you can arrive through Poto Tano, the ferry port linking Lombok with Sumbawa. The crossing offers scenic views of the surrounding islands, making the journey part of the adventure. From Poto Tano, it’s just a 30-minute car ride to Mocean Resort, ideal for guests arriving from Lombok or those enjoying an island-hopping itinerary. With ocean breezes and our team ready to welcome you, this route combines convenience with a memorable start to your stay.

headings: Pro Tips for a Smooth Arrival
sections.text: Pro Tips for a Smooth Arrival Plan your arrival in advance to make your journey as smooth as possible. Check flight options into Sumbawa Besar Airport (SWQ) or review ferry schedules from Lombok to ensure you avoid unnecessary delays. For longer rides, it’s a good idea to pack a few essentials such as light snacks, bottled water, and sunscreen so you stay comfortable along the way. Don’t forget to share your exact arrival details with our team so transfers are arranged and waiting for you upon landing or docking. Whenever possible, aim to arrive during daylight hours, as it not only makes navigation easier but also allows you to take in the stunning island scenery right from the start. By preparing ahead, your first impression of Mocean Beach Resort will be relaxed, seamless, and truly memorable.

sections.text: FAQ Beach Resort FAQ Is Mocean Beach Resort right on the beach? Yes. The pool, restaurant, lounge and yoga chalet sit on the shoreline of Pantai Moro. The rooms face tropical gardens a few steps back from the sand. Do the rooms have sea views? The rooms look onto the gardens. For sea views, the pool deck and Mutiara restaurant face the ocean directly. Is the resort good for families? Yes. Rooms take up to three guests and a cot or child’s fold-out bed can be added. The house reef has shallow snorkeling and the pool is right by the beach.
